Below you’ll find a “tool‑box” of ways to pull **detailed interface data**—from simple shell one‑liners all the way up to programmatic access through SNMP, NETCONF/YANG, or vendor‑specific APIs. Pick the method that matches your environment: | Platform / Context | What you’re looking at | Typical Commands / Calls | |--------------------|------------------------|--------------------------| | **Linux host** | Interface name (`eth0`, `ens5f1`) – MAC, MTU, state, traffic counters, driver details | ```bash
ip link show eth0 # basic flags & MAC
ip -s link show eth0 # stats + mtu
ethtool -i eth0 # driver & firmware
cat /sys/class/net/eth0/device/modalias # hardware ID``` | | **macOS** | Same as above plus Bonjour services | ```bash
networksetup -getinfo Ethernet # human‑readable summary
ifconfig en0 # low‑level view``` | | **Windows CMD** | NIC properties | ```cmd\nwmic nic where Name="Ethernet" get *\n``` or `netsh interface ip show addresses "Local Area Connection"` | | **PowerShell** | Rich object output | ```powershell\nGet-NetAdapter -Name "Ethernet"\nGet-CimInstance Win32_NetworkAdapterConfiguration | Where-Object {$_.Description -eq "Ethernet"}\n``` | | **Cisco IOS / NX‑OS** | Switch/router port details | ```cisco-ios\nshow interface GigabitEthernet1/0/24 detail\n``` | | **Juniper Junos** | Port description, speed, errors | ```juniper-junos\nshow interfaces ge-0/0/1 extensive\n``` | | **Arista EOS** | Detailed port metrics | ```arista-eos\nshow interface ethernet1 switchport\n``` | | **SNMP** | Generic across devices | ```snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifTable\n``` | | **NETCONF/YANG** | Structured XML/JSON | ```xml\n\n``` | | **RESTful API (e.g., Arista CloudVision)** | Endpoint returns JSON | ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.cloudvision.arista.com/v1/interfaces/\n``` | --- ### 1️⃣ Quick CLI Cheatsheet #### Linux ```bash # Basic info + MAC ip link show dev eth0 # Stats + MTU ip -s link show dev eth0 # Driver & firmware ethtool -i eth0 # Hardware IDs udevadm info --query=all --name=/dev/mii_eth0 | grep ID_MODEL_ID ``` #### macOS ```bash # Human readable networksetup -getinfo Ethernet # Low level sudo ifconfig en0 ``` #### Windows ```bat rem Get all adapter attributes wmic nic where Name="Ethernet" get * rem Show IPv4 configuration netsh interface ip show addresses "Local Area Connection" ``` #### PowerShell ```powershell # Adapter overview Get-NetAdapter -Physical | Format-List * # Full CIM instance Get-CimInstance Win32_NetworkAdapterConfiguration | Where-Object { $_.IPEnabled } | Format-List * ``` --- ### 2️⃣ Vendor‑Specific Detail Retrieval | Vendor | Command | Output Highlights | |--------|---------|-------------------| | **Cisco IOS** | `show interface GiX/X/X` | Status, duplex, speed, error counts, VLAN membership | | **NX‑OS** | `show interface mgmt0` | Management port specifics | | **Juniper** | `show interfaces ge-X/X/X terse` | Speed, admin/up/down, packet stats | | **Arista** | `show interface EthernetX` | LACP, flow control, port-channel members | If you have many switches, consider automating with Ansible’s `ios_interface_facts` module or similar. --- ### 3️⃣ Programmatic Access #### A) Using SNMP (Python) ```python import sys from pysnmp.hlapi import * def snmp_walk(oid): iterator = nextCmd( SnmpEngine(), CommunityData('public', mpModel=1), # v2c UdpTransportTarget(('192.168.1.10', 161)), ContextData(), ObjectType(ObjectIdentity(oid)) ) for errorIndication, errorStatus, _, varBinds in iterator: if errorIndication: print(errorIndication) break elif errorStatus: print('%s at %s' % ( errorStatus.prettyPrint(), errorIndex.prettyPrint() )) break else: for varBind in varBinds: print(varBind[0], '=', varBind[1]) if __name__ == "__main__": snmp_walk('IF-MIB::ifDescr') ``` *Replace `'192.168.1.10'` and community string accordingly.* #### B) Using NETCONF/YANG (Python) ```python from ncclient import manager with manager.connect(host='router.example.net', port=830, username='admin', password='pwd', hostkey_verify=False) as m: netconf_filter = """ """ reply = m.dispatch(netconf_filter.encode()) print(reply.xml) ``` #### C) Using RestConf / REST API ```bash curl -k \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -u admin:pwd \ https://switch.example.net/restconf/data/Cisco-IETF-Interfaces:interfaces/interface= ``` --- ### 4️⃣ Pulling Data into a Dashboard Once you’ve got raw data, feed it into Grafana, Kibana, or even Excel: | Tool | How | |------|-----| | **Grafana** | InfluxDB → Prometheus exporter (node_exporter) → Grafana panel | | **Kibana** | Logstash ingest pipeline parsing SNMP traps → Elasticsearch index | | **Excel** | Import CSV generated by `csvkit` or `pandas.read_csv()` | --- ### 5️⃣ Common Pitfalls & Tips | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | No `ethtool` installed | `apt-get install ethtool` (Debian/Ubuntu) or `yum install ethtool` (CentOS/RHEL) | | Permissions denied on `/proc/net/dev` | Run as root or add current user to `adm` group | | SNMP walk times out | Verify firewall allows UDP 161 inbound/outbound | | Wrong OID | Double‑check MIB files (`ls /usr/share/snmp/mibs/*.txt`) | | Mixed naming conventions | Normalize names (`eth0` vs `enp0s25`) before comparison | --- ## TL;DR Cheat Sheet ```text # Linux quick facts $ ip link show eth0 $ ip -s link show eth0 $ ethtool -i eth0 # Windows PowerShell PS> Get-NetAdapter -Name "Ethernet" # Cisco router Router# show interface gi1/0/48 detail # SNMP python snippet >>> snmp_walk("IF-MIB::ifOperStatus") ``` Feel free to let me know what platform or specific metric you’re after, and I can drill down further!
